1.name: Body
1.note: The fixed housing. The upper halves of the pin chambers are drilled in it, and its join with the plug is the shear line.

2.name: Plug
2.note: The rotating core with the keyway. It turns only when every pin gap sits on the shear line: the AND of all five checks.

3.name: Key pin 1
3.note: Rests on the key. Its length is cut for one depth, so the right key lifts its top to the shear line.

4.name: Key pin 2
4.note: Rests on the key. Its length is cut for one depth, so the right key lifts its top to the shear line.

5.name: Key pin 3
5.note: Rests on the key. With a key one cut wrong this pin sits low, its driver straddles the line and the plug will not turn.

6.name: Key pin 4
6.note: Rests on the key. Its length is cut for one depth, so the right key lifts its top to the shear line.

7.name: Key pin 5
7.note: Rests on the key. Its length is cut for one depth, so the right key lifts its top to the shear line.

8.name: Driver pin
8.note: Sits on each key pin and crosses the shear line when the pin is wrong. The plug is free only when the gap between the two lies on the line.

9.name: Pin spring
9.note: Pushes each driver and key pin down onto the key, and back into the plug when the key is withdrawn.

10.name: Chamber cap
10.note: Pressed into the top of each chamber to close it and give the pin spring something to push against.

11.name: Cam
11.note: Turns with the plug and carries the turn out to the lock bolt.

12.name: Retaining washer
12.note: Clips into a groove on the plug's tail to hold the cam and plug in place.

13.name: Anti-drill pin
13.note: A hardened pin set in the plug face. It blunts a drill aimed at the pins, so the lock cannot simply be drilled open.

14.name: Fixing screw
14.note: Passes through the cylinder to fix it in the door lock.

15.name: Key
15.note: The secret. Each cut is one of seven depths in 0.5 mm steps and lifts its key pin by that amount.

16.name: Thrust washer
16.note: Takes the axial load between the plug and the cam, so the plug turns freely.
